sentences.text: Challenging judgment and award dated 10.11.2016 passed by II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short) in MVC no.592/2015, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Sri Mahantesh Patil, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by owner challenging dismissal of claim petition against insurer and fastening liability on him.

It was submitted that as per claim petition, on 13.04.2015, Smt.Ningamma was traveling in Auto bearing Reg.no.KA-36/A- NC: 2023:KHC-K:7329 9423 towards Manvi when its driver drove it in rash and negligent manner and caused accident leading to her death.
Hence, claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act was filed against owner and insurer of Auto.

Lingangouda vs Hanumanth And Ors on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32988287/
2 3.
On contest, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant no.1 as PW.1 and Exs.P1 to 8 were marked.
Respondents examined official of insurer as RW.1 and Exs.R1 to 4 were marked.
4. On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Auto by its driver and claimant was entitled for Rs.5,00,000/- as compensation.
But only on ground that driver of Auto did not have 'transport' endorsement on his driving licence, while he was driving passenger Auto, tribunal fastened liability on owner instead of insurer.

Assailing same, it was submitted that in view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan v/s Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in 2017 (14) SCC 663, reason assigned by tribunal would be contrary to law and call for interference.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan v/s Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in 2017 (14) SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
6. From above submission, since owner is in appeal challenging finding of tribunal on liability

, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether tribunal was justified in dismissing claim petition against insurer?"
7.
Admittedly, vehicle involved in accident is Auto rickshaw which would be a light motor vehicle.
Exs.P7 and Ex.R3 - driving licence extracts would indicate that as on date of accident, driver of Auto had valid driving licence to drive light motor vehicle.

Though he did not have 'transport'
endorsement, said requirement would stand diluted in view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan's case (supra).
Thus, insurer cannot escape liability.
Therefore, finding of tribunal holding owner liable would be unjustified.
Hence, point for consideration is answered in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7329 ORDER i. Appeal is allowed.
Dismissal of claim petition against insurer is set-aside.
ii. Impugned judgment and award dated 10.11.2016 passed by II Additional and Sessions Judge, Raichur is modified and respondent no.2 - insurer is held liable to pay compensation to claimant.

entities.text: II Additional and Sessions Judge, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: iii. Amount in deposit is ordered to be refunded to appellant - owner.
